text.title: Deal with EU not dependent on tuition fees agreement, Miliband says
text.body_text: - Published A deal agreed between the UK and the European Union on Friday will come into force regardless of whether the two sides can negotiate a separate tuition fees agreement, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has told the BBC.…
text.summary: Brussels sources had previously suggested the bloc might not apply the wider deal until fees were lowered for EU students in Britain.

text.title: ‘In the office, there was a sharp intake of breath’: why has the BBC decided to celebrate Christmas earlier than ever?
text.body_text: Traditionally, around this time of year, people remark that Christmas feels as though it’s coming earlier than ever. In the BBC’s case, it actually is. Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Christmas Fishing, The Repair Shop at Christmas and other festive BBC specials will be available to watch on iPlayer from 27 November, up to a month before these shows debut on…
text.summary: Festive specials are being released on the iPlayer as much as a month before the big day. Is this a dire flouting of tradition – or a welcome modernisation? TV insiders analyse the change Traditionally, around this time of year, people remark that Christmas feels as though it’s coming earlier than ever. In the BBC’s case, it actually is. Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Christmas Fishing, The Repair Shop at Christmas and other festive BBC specials will be available to watch on iPlayer from 27 November, up to a month before these shows debut on the television itself. This means you can watch Mary Berry avidly talk about the joy of eating mince pies, followed by a Christmas-themed murder in the Caribbean in Death in Paradise, well before the tree is up (unless, of course, you put up your tree earlier than ever, too). audio.title: How a viral video gave a huge boost to new gene therapy
audio.description: Sanfilippo syndrome is a rare and degenerative disease that can be fatal by the time someone reaches their teens. So the O’Neill family knew they didn’t have much time after learning their 4-year old daughter, Eliza, had it. At the time no treatment existed, and the world of drug development had its eyes on more common illnesses. So the family took an all hands on deck, unusual approach to directly raise money and boost medical research. NPR pharmaceutical correspondent Sydney Lupkin shares what happened next, and what she learned from the O’Neills story about the promises and challenges of drug development.
